scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: The dispute volume rose from about 600 tickets in June/July to over 1,100 in August and 1,260 in September, confirming a roughly doubling of tickets since August.
The observation shows that disputed bills include both estimated (1,240) and actual (1,785) meter reads, indicating that disputes are not limited to estimated reads.
The CRM shows dispute tickets are answered within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3‑day SLA) despite a high volume of 2,440 tickets, indicating response speed is not the bottleneck.
Field route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating that manual meter reads are not being completed as planned, which can lead to estimated bills and disputes.
The tariff change log in the billing database contains no records, indicating that no tariff changes were logged during the observed period.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Staffing shortage of three meter readers since July has caused delayed field routes, leading to estimated bills for affected customers.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports no tariff changes this year, indicating that tariff modifications are not a source of the recent dispute surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that the utility can request route priority changes, but such changes must be executed after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, indicating a human‑approval step for route updates.

E-09.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned, enabling retrieval of AMI read data that can be used to supplement manual reads and reduce estimated bill generation.

The observation shows that among disputed estimated bills, 1,184 had AMI reads taken before the billing cutoff but were rejected due to high consumption, while 56 had no AMI read received. This indicates that AMI data is available but not used because of validation issues, not solely because of missing manual reads.

trace.summary: Deterministic rules can implement the feasible AMI‑read configuration and simple threshold monitoring; LLM reasoning helps interpret stakeholder claims and handle ambiguous exceptions; autonomous iteration can refine route schedules and AMI‑read weighting based on real‑time data; residual exceptions remain for non‑AMI meters and unexpected data gaps; detection is needed to monitor route completion and AMI‑read ingestion.

structural_remedies.description: Hire three additional meter readers to eliminate the field staffing shortage reported in E-06 and CL-02, thereby increasing manual read capacity and improving route completion toward the 0.95 target (F-04).
structural_remedies.rationale: Hiring and onboarding cannot be completed within the remaining 225 minutes.; residual gap: Even with added staff, route completion may remain below target due to scheduling or non-AMI meter gaps; supplemental AMI reads or route optimization may still be needed.

structural_remedies.description: Configure the billing import process to accept AMI register reads from DA-MDMS as primary inputs, reducing reliance on manual reads and thus lowering estimated bill generation (E-02, DA-MDMS, H-MDMS-BILL).
structural_remedies.rationale: Configuration changes can be made within the remaining time and do not violate K-BILLWRITE or K-DISPATCH.; residual gap: AMI coverage is not universal; non-AMI meters may still generate estimated bills if manual reads remain incomplete.
